evidence.quote: Fiscal Year 2025 Compared with Fiscal Year 2024

input.label: SUPPORTED
input.reasoning_summary: After reviewing the weaknesses, my initial verdict remains SUPPORTED. W1 and W3 correctly note that the claim is straightforward and the evidence directly supports it - the 10-K filing shows net income grew 16% from FY2024 ($88,136M) to FY2025 ($101,832M), which exceeds the claimed 10% threshold. W2 raised a concern about one-time items, but upon examination, the evidence actually refutes this as a weakness: E4 shows that one-time losses (increased investment losses and other losses including OpenAI equity method losses) actually worked AGAINST net income growth in FY2025, meaning these items made the comparison less favorable, not more favorable. The 16% growth occurred despite these headwinds, not because of artificial inflation. The claim is purely numeric with no causal attribution, and the evidence unambiguously supports that net income increased by more than 10% (specifically 16%) comparing FY2025 to FY2024.
input.change_reason: No change. All three weaknesses were refuted by the evidence. The claim is clearly supported by the 16% year-over-year net income growth shown in the 10-K filing.
